items.title: Flagship Rural Development Schemes
items.body:
## What rural development covers

Rural development is a **multi-dimensional effort** to raise rural incomes and quality of life through **infrastructure, credit, wage/self-employment, housing, sanitation and food security**, delivered largely via the three-tier **Panchayati Raj** system (73rd Amendment, 1992) under the **Ministry of Rural Development**.

## Key central schemes

| Scheme | Year | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| MGNREGA | 2005 | Legal guarantee of 100 days unskilled wage employment per rural household |
| PMGSY | 2000 | All-weather roads to unconnected habitations |
| PMAY-Gramin | 2016 | Pucca houses (replaced Indira Awaas Yojana) |
| DAY-NRLM (Aajeevika) | 2011 | Women SHG-based livelihoods |
| DDU-GKY | 2014 | Placement-linked skilling of rural youth |
| SAGY | 2014 | MPs adopt & develop model villages via convergence |

- **IRDP (1978-80)** was the pioneering self-employment anti-poverty programme, later subsumed under SGSY and then NRLM.
- Schemes **converge**: PMAY-G houses use SBM toilets and MGNREGA labour.
keyPoints: MGNREGA (2005) guarantees 100 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household, with one-third women.
PMGSY (2000) builds all-weather rural roads; PMAY-Gramin (2016) provides pucca houses, replacing Indira Awaas Yojana.
DAY-NRLM/Aajeevika (2011) mobilises rural women into SHGs; DDU-GKY (2014) gives placement-linked skilling.
SAGY (2014) has MPs adopt Gram Panchayats and develop them through convergence, with no separate fund.
IRDP (1978-80) was the early self-employment anti-poverty scheme, later merged into SGSY then NRLM.
items.mnemonic: Rural 'MPPDDS' = MGNREGA, PMGSY, PMAY-G, DAY-NRLM, DDU-GKY, SAGY.
items.source: Ministry of Rural Development / PIB — rural development schemes

items.title: Urban Development Missions (2015 onwards)
items.body:
## The 2015 urban mission cluster

After the **JNNURM (2005)** legacy mission wound down, three flagship urban missions were launched in 2015 under the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)**:

| Mission | Coverage | Thrust |
|---|---|---|
| Smart Cities Mission | 100 cities | Area-based development + pan-city smart solution, executed via an SPV |
| AMRUT | 500 cities/towns (1 lakh+) | Water supply, sewerage, drainage, transport, green spaces |
| PMAY-Urban | Urban poor | 'Housing for All' — 4 verticals ISSR, CLSS, AHP, BLC |

- **HRIDAY (2015)** funded heritage-city development (Varanasi, Amaravati, Ajmer, Puri, etc.).
- **AMRUT 2.0 (2021)** targets universal tap-water and sewerage coverage; **PMAY-U 2.0 (2024)** adds ~1 crore urban houses.
- **DAY-NULM** covers urban SHGs, self-employment, homeless shelters and street vendors (with **PM SVANidhi**, 2020, for vendor credit).
keyPoints: Smart Cities Mission (2015) targets 100 cities via area-based + pan-city development through an SPV.
AMRUT (2015) covers 500 towns with water supply as top priority; AMRUT 2.0 (2021) targets universal water/sewerage.
PMAY-Urban has four verticals — ISSR, CLSS, AHP, BLC; PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) adds about 1 crore houses.
HRIDAY (2015) funded heritage-city development; JNNURM (2005) was the predecessor urban-reform mission.
DAY-NULM handles urban livelihoods, shelters and street vendors, complemented by PM SVANidhi (2020).
items.mnemonic: Urban 'SAPH' = Smart Cities, AMRUT, PMAY-U, HRIDAY (+ NULM for livelihoods).
items.source: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs / PIB — urban missions

items.title: Swachh Bharat Mission & Sanitation
items.body:
## Sanitation as a development lever

The **Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM)**, launched **2 October 2014**, aimed at an **Open Defecation Free (ODF) India** through mass toilet construction and behaviour change.

- **Two wings:** SBM-Gramin (Ministry of Jal Shakti) and SBM-Urban (MoHUA).
- India was declared **ODF in October 2019** (Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary).
- **SBM 2.0 (2021)** shifts focus to **ODF-Plus** — sustaining ODF, plus solid and liquid waste management, plastic-waste and greywater management.
- Complements PMAY (every house with a toilet) and improves rural health and women's safety/dignity.
keyPoints: SBM launched 2 October 2014 to make India Open Defecation Free (ODF).
SBM-Gramin is under Ministry of Jal Shakti; SBM-Urban under MoHUA.
India declared ODF in October 2019.
SBM 2.0 (2021) focuses on ODF-Plus — solid/liquid, plastic and greywater waste management.
SBM converges with PMAY so that houses include toilets, aiding health and women's safety.

items.title: Urbanisation — Definition, Trends & Challenges
items.body:
## Defining 'urban' (Census of India)

An **urban area** = all **statutory towns** (with a municipality/corporation/notified area/cantonment) **plus census towns** that satisfy all three criteria:

1. **Population ≥ 5,000**
2. **Density ≥ 400 persons per sq km**
3. **≥ 75% of male working population in non-agricultural work**

## Trends & challenges

- Urban population share was about **31% (Census 2011)** and is projected to keep rising toward ~40% by around 2030.
- Rapid, unplanned urbanisation brings **slums and informal settlements, distress migration, solid-waste and sewage burdens, congestion, and strain on housing and water**.
- Policy response = the mission cluster (Smart Cities, AMRUT, PMAY-U, SBM-U) plus urban-local-body reforms under the **74th Amendment (1992)**.
keyPoints: Urban area = statutory towns + census towns meeting population, density and non-agri workforce criteria.
Census-town criteria: population >= 5,000; density >= 400 per sq km; >= 75% male workers in non-agriculture.
Census 2011 urban share was about 31%, projected to rise toward ~40% by 2030.
Challenges: slums, distress migration, solid-waste/sewage load, congestion and housing shortage.
74th Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to urban local bodies (Part IX-A, Twelfth Schedule).

items.title: Rural Credit, Institutions, Land Records & Labour Concepts
items.body:
## Rural credit institutions

| Institution | Role |
|---|---|
| **NABARD** (1982) | Apex — **refinances** banks; does NOT lend directly to farmers; pioneered **SHG-Bank Linkage (1992)** |
| **RRBs** | Give **direct** credit to rural households (small farmers, artisans) |
| **Land Development Banks** | Give **direct** long-term (mortgage) credit |
| Cooperatives | PACS → DCCB → State Coop Bank; **PACS** are village primary societies |

## Credit-planning machinery

- **Lead Bank Scheme (1969)** — each **district is 'adopted' by a lead bank** for intensive credit development (Gadgil/Nariman).
- **Service Area Approach (1989)** — operates **under the Lead Bank Scheme**; assigns villages to bank branches for planned rural lending.
- **DRDA (District Rural Development Agency)** — coordinates anti-poverty programmes and monitors fund utilisation at district level.

## Labour & poverty concepts

- **Disguised unemployment** — more workers than needed, so the **marginal productivity of labour is zero** (typical of agriculture/family farms).
- **Demographic dividend** — a young workforce boosts growth **only if backed by skilling, health and jobs**.
- **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** — by **OPHI + UNDP**; measures deprivation in **health, education and standard of living** at the household level; India has a **National MPI (NITI Aayog)**.

## Land records — DILRMP

- The **Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP)** aims at **conclusive land titling** through **digitisation of cadastral maps** and **transliteration of Records of Rights (RoR) into Constitution-recognised languages**; it assigns a unique land-parcel ID (**ULPIN / Bhu-Aadhaar**).
- *Exam note:* answer keys have treated the claim that it is **'100% centrally funded'** as **incorrect** (it began as a cost-shared Centrally Sponsored Scheme) — the safe hinge-facts are the cadastral-map and RoR-transliteration components.
keyPoints: NABARD (1982) refinances banks and pioneered SHG-Bank Linkage (1992); it does NOT lend directly — RRBs and Land Development Banks give direct rural credit.
Lead Bank Scheme (1969): each district is adopted by a lead bank; Service Area Approach (1989) operates under it.
DRDA coordinates district anti-poverty programmes and monitors fund utilisation.
Disguised unemployment = marginal productivity of labour is zero; demographic dividend needs skilling/health/jobs.
MPI (OPHI + UNDP) measures health, education and living-standard deprivation; India has a National MPI (NITI Aayog).
DILRMP digitises cadastral maps and transliterates RoR to recognised languages (ULPIN/Bhu-Aadhaar); the '100% central funding' claim is treated as incorrect by answer keys.
items.mnemonic: Direct rural credit = RRB + LDB; NABARD only RE-finances (R for Refinance).
items.source: NABARD; RBI — Lead Bank Scheme/Service Area Approach; Ministry of Rural Development — DRDA; DoLR — DILRMP; OPHI-UNDP MPI

items.title: Social-Sector Convergence for Inclusive Development
items.body:
## Why social sectors are development instruments

Inclusive rural development needs **human-capital and social-security convergence**, not schemes alone. Education, nutrition, maternal health and decentralised planning are treated as **instruments of inclusive growth**.

## Education & nutrition

- **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009** — operationalises **Article 21A**; guarantees **free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14**, a core inclusive-growth/human-capital instrument (with 25% EWS seats in private schools).
- **Mid-Day Meal Scheme**, now **PM POSHAN (2021)** — hot cooked meals in government schools to improve **enrolment, retention and child nutrition** simultaneously.

## Maternal & child health (NRHM convergence)

- **ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist)** — village health volunteer under the **NRHM/NHM (2005)**; **accompanies women for antenatal care and immunisation, gives nutrition/health counselling**, but **does NOT conduct deliveries herself**.
- **Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)** — a **conditional cash-transfer** under NRHM promoting **institutional (facility) deliveries** to cut maternal/infant mortality.
- *Scope note:* ASHA and JSY are **health-mission** interventions that **converge with** rural development but are administered by the health ministry.

## Decentralised planning & poverty lines

- **District Planning Committees (DPCs)** — mandated by **Article 243ZD**; **consolidate the plans of panchayats and municipalities** into a district development plan.
- **Poverty-line committees:** **Tendulkar Committee (2009)** and **Rangarajan Committee (2014)** revised India's poverty-line methodology.
keyPoints: RTE Act 2009 operationalises Article 21A — free and compulsory education for ages 6-14; a core inclusive-growth/human-capital instrument.
Mid-Day Meal, now PM POSHAN (2021), links school nutrition with enrolment and retention.
ASHA (NRHM/NHM 2005) accompanies women for antenatal care and immunisation and gives nutrition counselling, but does NOT conduct deliveries.
Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a conditional cash transfer under NRHM promoting institutional deliveries.
District Planning Committees (Article 243ZD) consolidate panchayat and municipality plans into a district plan.
Tendulkar (2009) and Rangarajan (2014) committees revised India's poverty-line methodology.
items.mnemonic: Convergence 'RAJD' = RTE, ASHA/JSY, PM POSHAN, DPCs.
items.source: MoE — RTE/PM POSHAN; MoHFW — NRHM (ASHA, JSY); Constitution Art 243ZD; Tendulkar/Rangarajan reports

items.title: Andhra Pradesh — Rural & Urban Development Initiatives
items.body:
## AP rural development

- **SERP (Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty)** ran large-scale **women's SHG mobilisation** under **Velugu / Indira Kranthi Patham (IKP)**, building on the earlier **DWCRA** model — a nationally recognised community-driven poverty-reduction approach.
- SHG federations link to **DAY-NRLM** for bank credit, and to livelihood, dairy and micro-enterprise activities.
- Rural housing, drinking water and road connectivity are delivered through the central schemes (PMAY-G, Jal Jeevan Mission, PMGSY) plus state programmes.

## AP urban development

- **MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas)** is the urban counterpart of SERP, driving **urban SHGs, DAY-NULM and slum-poor livelihoods**.
- AP cities feature in national missions — **Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Tirupati** under Smart Cities/AMRUT — and the state is developing its capital region **Amaravati**.
- e-governance delivery through **MeeSeva/citizen-service centres** supports both rural and urban service access.
keyPoints: AP's SERP led women's SHG mobilisation under Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham, building on DWCRA.
AP SHG federations link with DAY-NRLM for credit and livelihoods.
MEPMA is AP's urban-poverty agency implementing urban SHGs and DAY-NULM.
Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Tirupati feature in Smart Cities/AMRUT; Amaravati is the capital-region project.
MeeSeva citizen-service e-governance supports service delivery across rural and urban AP.
items.source: Government of Andhra Pradesh — SERP, MEPMA, Municipal Administration & Rural Development
